title: Tailwind CSS
description: Install and configure Tailwind CSS v4 with the CSS-first theme, and know the utility-first trade-offs.

data.text: Tailwind is a utility-first framework: instead of naming components in CSS, you compose small utility classes in markup. Tailwind then generates only the utilities you actually use, so the shipped CSS stays tiny.

data.title: Set up Tailwind v4 with PostCSS
data.content: v4 replaced the JavaScript config with CSS-first configuration.
data.code:
npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss postcss
# or with the Vite plugin
npm install -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite

data.caption: src/app.css — one import does the work in v4

data.text: The `@theme` block defines design tokens that become both CSS custom properties and utilities (`bg-brand`, `font-display`, `rounded-card`). There is no `content` array in v4 — source detection is automatic and ignores `.gitignore`d files.

data.caption: Using utilities and variants

data.text: Long class strings are the usual complaint. Extract a React component when the markup repeats, and reach for `@utility` (v4) or `@apply` only when a raw CSS rule is genuinely clearer. Never invent class names dynamically — Tailwind scans source text, so `` `bg-${color}-500` `` produces no CSS.

data.caption: A custom utility in v4

data.title: Dynamic class names do not exist
data.text: Template-literal class names are invisible to the scanner. Map variants to complete class strings (or use `clsx` plus a lookup object) so every class appears literally in the source.

terms.definition: A single-purpose class such as p-4 or text-sm that maps to one CSS declaration.
Tailwind v4 CSS block that defines design tokens and generates matching utilities.
A prefix such as md:, hover:, or dark: that applies a utility conditionally.
Tailwind's automatic scan of source files to decide which utilities to emit.

items.question: Does Tailwind make markup unreadable?
items.answer: It moves style decisions from CSS files into components, which is often an improvement for component libraries. When declarations repeat, extract a component rather than fighting the framework.

items.question: Do I still need PostCSS?
items.answer: With Tailwind v4 you typically use the Vite plugin, which is faster. The PostCSS plugin remains the integration point for Webpack, Next.js, and plain build pipelines.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Explain that only used utilities are generated, that class names must be static for detection, and how @theme replaces the old JavaScript config.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Tailwind generates only the utilities present in your source.
v4 configures the theme in CSS with @theme; there is no content array.
Extract components for repeated class strings; avoid @apply by default.
Dynamic class names produce no CSS — always use complete literal strings.
data.takeaway: Tailwind is a build-time tool: nothing is shipped that you did not use.
